The additional lighting in the backyard areas should also have a positive impact in this regard. Demolition, rehabilitation and code enforcement will also eliminate vacant or abandoned structures where crime could breed. Code enforcement, which is a form of police power, will require that abandoned structures be thoroughly cleaned out and boarded up to prevent unauthorized entrance to the building prior to its disposition—demolition or rehabilitation.
Since the area is patroled by cruiser and by foot, the improved streets, sidewalks and backyard walkways will be of some minor positive value.
i. Fire Protection
During the execution stages of the project, properties that are acquired, even though boarded up as required by local law, will remain as fire hazards until razed. This represents a negative factor as it relates to fire protection for the area.
Once these structures are removed and population density is decreased, principally in the northeastern areas of the project, fire fighting facilities will be better able to handle fires in the project area.
Access to the area with fire fighting equipment will also be improved as the result of improved sidewalks, walkways, and streets.
The new flood plain ordinances will also help to prevent the possibility of fires caused by electrical systems in new structures should flooding reoccur.
Stricter code enforcement will impact the demands on fire fighting facilities by reducing the number of potentially dangerous or illegally installed heating systems and electrical systems.
j. Solid Waste Collection
The solid waste collection will be impacted, in a negative respect, during the construction demolition periods, but in the long run the service will benefit from the project improvements and the redistribution of population.
